laws.rule: Bavaria bans smoking, heating or vaping cannabis in beer gardens and other outdoor areas of bars and restaurants, in festival tents and across Volksfest grounds (such as Oktoberfest), on top of the federal bans near minors, schools and in pedestrian zones from 7 am to 8 pm.

Berchtesgaden National Park (Bavarian Alps): stay on the paths, keep dogs on a lead, and take rubbish out. Camping and sleeping outdoors are prohibited, and so are fires. Bikes are allowed only on approved routes. Boating on the park's waters is prohibited. Rangers patrol all year and fines are issued for breaches. The park says people found camping at Salet, Kessel or St. Bartholomä on the Königssee after the last boat have been taken back by a special boat, at high cost to them.

Feiertagsgesetz (FTG) Art. 3 and Art. 7: stille Tage (silent days)
laws.rule: Bavaria protects nine 'silent days' (stille Tage): Ash Wednesday, Maundy Thursday, Good Friday, Holy Saturday, All Saints (1 November), Volkstrauertag (second Sunday before Advent), Totensonntag, Buss- und Bettag and Christmas Eve. The protection runs from 2 am to midnight; on Good Friday and Holy Saturday it starts at midnight (0:00), and on Christmas Eve it starts at 2 pm. Public entertainment events are allowed on those days only if they keep a serious character. Sport events are allowed, except on Good Friday and Buss- und Bettag. On Good Friday any music (live or played) is banned in rooms that serve drinks. Art. 7 allows a fine of up to EUR 10,000 (about A$15,890 at A$1 = EUR 0.6293, RBA 30 Oct 2026) for holding an event that lacks the serious character, for sport on the two banned days, and for music in a bar on Good Friday.
laws.penalty_signal: Fine up to EUR 10,000 (about A$15,890) on the organiser (Art. 7); the Act names no separate fine for a guest.

laws.heading: Feiertagsgesetz (FTG) Art. 7: noise near churches
laws.rule: On Sundays and public holidays, avoidable noisy acts near a church during the usual time of the main church service are an offence if they are likely to disturb the service; so are public entertainment events or drives (Treibjagden, hunts) then (Art. 2(2) and Art. 7 Nr. 2). On Buss- und Bettag the main-service window is 7 am to 11 am (Art. 4 and Art. 7 Nr. 5). Fine up to EUR 10,000 (about A$15,890, RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293).

laws.heading: Gesundheitsschutzgesetz (GSG) Art. 2, Art. 3 and Art. 10
laws.rule: Bavaria bans smoking tobacco and cannabis indoors in public buildings, schools and children's facilities (including playgrounds), adult education, health facilities, homes, culture and leisure venues, sports venues, bars and restaurants (Gaststatten) and commercial airports (Art. 2 and Art. 3(1) sentence 1). In children's and youth facilities the ban also covers the grounds (Art. 3(1) sentence 2). Art. 5 and Art. 6 allow some exceptions, such as separate smoking rooms. The Act's smoking ban covers tobacco products and cannabis products; it does not mention nicotine e-cigarettes (heating or vaping cannabis counts as smoking). A person who smokes where it is banned can be fined; on a repeat the fine can reach EUR 5,000 (about A$7,946, RBA 30 Oct 2026).
laws.penalty_signal: Fine; up to EUR 5,000 on a repeat (Art. 10(1)).

laws.heading: Gesundheitsschutzgesetz (GSG) Art. 10(2): cannabis smoking fines
laws.rule: Smoking, heating or vaporising cannabis where Bavaria bans it (Art. 3(1) and (2), which includes the beer-garden, Volksfest and Maximilianeum areas) can be fined up to EUR 1,500 (about A$2,384), and up to EUR 5,000 (about A$7,946) on a repeat (RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293).
laws.penalty_signal: Fine up to EUR 1,500; up to EUR 5,000 on a repeat.

laws.heading: Bayerisches Waldgesetz (BayWaldG) Art. 17, Art. 13 and Art. 46
laws.rule: In a forest, and within 100 m of one, you need a permit to light or run an open fire or fireplace (Art. 17(1)). You may not use open light, throw away burning or smouldering things, or leave a fire unattended (Art. 17(2)). Smoking in the forest is banned from 1 March to 31 October (Art. 17(3)). Fines: up to EUR 10,000 (about A$15,890) for an unpermitted fire or for breaking Art. 17(2); pitching a tent or caravan in the forest without authority, and smoking in the ban season, can also be fined (Art. 46(2) and (4)). Cycling, wheelchairs and riding in the forest are allowed only on roads and suitable paths (Art. 13(3)). AUD at A$1 = EUR 0.6293 (RBA 30 Oct 2026).
laws.penalty_signal: Fine up to EUR 10,000 for fire offences (Art. 46(2)).

items.text: Bavaria's Health Protection Act (Gesundheitsschutzgesetz, art. 3) bans smoking, heating or vaping cannabis wherever tobacco smoking is banned indoors, and also in the outdoor areas of restaurants and bars, including beer gardens, and across Volksfest grounds such as the Oktoberfest (rides, stalls, walkways and tents). Councils can add bans by ordinance for set crowded public places (art. 8). The fine is up to EUR 1,500 (about A$2,384), and up to EUR 5,000 (A$7,945) for a repeat (art. 10). AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293.

Bavaria's fines catalogue for the federal Cannabis Act (in force 1 April 2024) sets standard fines for a first deliberate offence: EUR 1,000 for using cannabis in the presence of minors (about A$1,589); EUR 500 for using it within 100 m of the entrance to schools, playgrounds, child and youth facilities or public sports grounds (A$795); EUR 300 in pedestrian zones between 7 am and 8 pm (A$477); and EUR 500 to EUR 1,000 for carrying more than 25 g, up to 30 g, away from home (A$795 to A$1,589). Fines double for a repeat of the same kind within three years and are halved for negligence. AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293.

On 24 November 2025 the Bavarian Administrative Court ruled that the state palace and gardens administration's ban on cannabis use in Munich's English Garden, Hofgarten and Finanzgarten is invalid (case 10 N 25.826), so the federal Cannabis Act rules apply there again. Beer gardens there remain under the Health Protection Act ban on outdoor dining areas.
